findings.reason: §7 check 5 (:277-280) pins `crew widen` as a live verb that must accept a non-running run and be the path `complete --accept-path` writes through, so a node cannot tombstone it without failing its own gate; the loose phrase names the reopening *procedure* (repair-status → widen → resume), not the verb.
findings.text: §7's flag list reads "`--reopen` replaces `repair-status`, `widen` and `resume`", but §7:266 excludes `widen` from the folded set ("`widen`, which this section keeps and widens") and §7:206 gives it new behaviour, so the same paragraph both retires and retains the verb

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — verified against the tree: `reckon/crew/claims.py` exposes `narrow_claim` (:90) and `release_claim` (128), contradicting nothing; `reckon/cli.py` re-exports `crew_preflight` (:221), `crew_redispatch` (:494), `crew_repair_status` (:500) and `crew_unwatch` (:524); `crew_watch` lives in `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py` (:3562); every §7 write-path module exists; and every folded-verb command string under `reckon/` (`preflight`/`resume-ready` in refusals.py, `check-manifest` in prompts.py, `repair-status` in recovery_classification.py, `repair-review` in obligations.py, `unwatch` in watch_unit.py, and the AGENTS.md rows) sits inside its folding node's fence, so no node hits the "file outside my write paths" stop the section anticipates.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each of the four nodes names a negative control that alters one of its successors' answers (§7:282) and the resume node names a second control routing `complete --accept-path` around the claim owner (:283); the leaf-count measure excludes tombstones and is taken at each node's own base (:273-276), so it cannot be satisfied by a stale figure.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §7 names no scratchpad or node-local path; the plan's landed evidence accumulates at `docs/evidence/archive/the-crew-surface-is-one-tool-and-a-few-verbs-landed.html`, which the §2/§3/§4 close comments already write.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol, filename or comment; the node ids (`cso-budget-family-folds` and the rest) and "the five shared ones" are plan-level dispatch identifiers, not code, and the files the nodes write are named by mechanism (`test_crew_families_fold.py`).
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the flag list says `--reopen` replaces `widen`, while the section's own tombstone carve-out keeps and widens `widen`.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each node folds one verb family; the `widen`/`complete --accept-path` claim change is the mechanism that makes `resume --reopen` work, and §7 check 5 (:277-280) carries it as part of the resume node's own gate.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §7's `depends-on` resolves to s6, and the node-level ordering for the two nodes that share §5's files (`reckon/crew/obligations.py`, `reckon/mcp.py`) is stated at §7:225 ("Only the third and fourth write a file §5 also writes, so they wait on §5") and enforced by the task-claim scope check rather than by a section edge that would over-hold the budget and watch nodes.
